email.subject: DBSA NRW panel: a specialist teaming question
email.initial:
Hi Tony,

The DBSA/WPO NRW contractor panel suggests a potential specialist pairing: WRP’s baseline and performance-measurement expertise with Ovarro’s leakage diagnostics. Your global leakage role looks relevant to testing that idea.

The compulsory briefing has passed. Any participation would first need an eligible contractor and a permitted subcontract route; neither firm is assumed to qualify as prime.

Would you be open to a 20-minute technical scoping discussion? If there is a fit, I’d ask both sides before arranging an introduction with Willem Wegelin. Neither side has committed.

If this is outside your remit, a referral would help. If you would prefer no further emails, please let me know.
followups:
Hi Tony,

Following up on DBSA/WPO NRW panel RFR001.2026. The first question is whether WRP Consulting Engineers would add a distinct, necessary work package. For your side, I had in mind: leak detection hardware, telemetry and leakage analytics work package.

Is that a useful scope to explore, or should I speak with another owner?

Hi Tony,

A practical agenda for the proposed WRP Consulting Engineers discussion would be: DMA baseline; logger coverage; leak validation; repair handoff; savings attribution; payment evidence. The output could be a one-page responsibility and evidence matrix before either firm spends time on a bid.

Which interface or qualification would you want to resolve first?

Hi Tony,

For DBSA/WPO NRW panel RFR001.2026, I would keep the commercial discussion tied to an agreed work package, acceptance criteria and delivery capacity. There is no assumed award, fee split or partner commitment.

Would you be comfortable assessing a possible introduction with Willem Wegelin at WRP Consulting Engineers, once the access and scope questions are resolved?

Hi Tony,

I’ll close this proposed WRP Consulting Engineers introduction for now. If a technical discussion would be useful, let me know the right owner and I can coordinate once both sides agree. If this tender is not a fit, a brief “not this one” is enough.

If you prefer no further emails, please let me know.
